questions.question: How is the universe described at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: It is pictured like a well-run kingdom or city where everything has an ordered job.

questions.question: What does the steady obedience of all creatures and groups in the universe point to?
questions.answer: It points to one complete rule and one all-encompassing authority.

questions.question: Which examples are given to show the wide range of Allah’s “armies”?
questions.answer: The passage mentions very tiny things like atoms, living plants and animals, and also the stars.

questions.question: Why does the passage say partners cannot share in Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: Because when more than one power tries to control the same matter, disorder and conflict follow.

questions.question: What everyday political examples are used to explain why shared rule leads to trouble?
questions.answer: It uses the examples of two kings in one land or two local leaders in one area.

questions.question: What shows that no rival power is actually interfering in the world?
questions.answer: The clear order seen everywhere, from very small things to huge heavenly bodies, shows that.

questions.question: Besides order, what other reason is given that sovereignty rejects rivals?
questions.answer: Rule has honor and majesty, so accepting an equal would go against that dignity.

questions.question: How does human behavior help explain this point about sovereignty?
questions.answer: Even weak human beings fight harshly over small, temporary power, which shows that authority does not welcome sharing.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from comparing human rule with Allah’s sovereignty?
questions.answer: If weak people refuse rivals over tiny power, then Allah would never allow anyone to share in His absolute rule.

questions.question: According to the passage, what relationship does Allah’s sovereignty have with His Lordship and Divinity?
questions.answer: His sovereignty is tied to His universal Lordship and His right to be worshipped alone.

questions.question: What attitude toward further discussion appears at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It says fuller proofs were explained elsewhere and directs the reader to those places.

questions.question: What is the main message of this whole section?
questions.answer: The order, unity, and dignity of rule in the universe show that Allah has no partner.

questions.question: What main truth is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: The truth of absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: What would someone notice by looking carefully at the cosmos?
questions.answer: They would see a world working like a successful state with wise organization and firm control.

questions.question: How are all things and living groups shown in that picture?
questions.answer: They are shown as carrying out their own assigned duties in obedience.

questions.question: What Qur’anic image is used to explain this organized universe?
questions.answer: The image of the heavens and the earth as Allah’s armies.

questions.question: What does the passage say about commands and laws in these “armies”?
questions.answer: They operate strongly and widely through every level of creation.

questions.question: How does the passage move from tiny things to giant ones to prove its point?
questions.answer: It starts with the smallest ranks, like atoms, and rises to plants, animals, and stars to show one rule covers all.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when many controlling hands push into one job?
questions.answer: The work becomes mixed up and loses order.

questions.question: What verse-based argument is used against many gods?
questions.answer: If there were other gods besides Allah in the heavens and earth, everything would fall into ruin.

questions.question: What evidence from the world argues against that ruin?
questions.answer: We actually see harmony and order everywhere instead of collapse and chaos.

questions.question: Which examples show that this order exists on both small and large scales?
questions.answer: The passage points to the wing of a fly, the cells in the body, the heavenly lights, and the planetary signs.

questions.question: Why is accepting a rival said to insult sovereignty itself?
questions.answer: Because true sovereignty carries greatness and honor that do not fit sharing with an equal.

questions.question: What final belief should a reader take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone rules all things, and nothing shares His authority.

questions.question: In this passage, what comparison helps readers understand the universe?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to a carefully governed kingdom or city.

questions.question: What does that comparison teach about the way the universe works?
questions.answer: It teaches that its parts are organized, purposeful, and under one command.

questions.question: Why are creatures described as obedient workers?
questions.answer: To show they act according to an ordered system, not random confusion.

questions.question: What is meant by calling parts of creation Allah’s armies?
questions.answer: It means every level of creation follows His command like disciplined forces under one ruler.

questions.question: How broad is this rule according to the passage?
questions.answer: It reaches everything from the smallest created things to the greatest heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What principle about leadership is used to argue against polytheism?
questions.answer: One area cannot stay orderly if two separate rulers both claim control over it.

questions.question: What would happen to a land with two kings, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Its order would break down and be replaced by confusion.

questions.question: How does the actual condition of the universe answer that imaginary situation?
questions.answer: The universe shows stable order, so it is not being ruled by competing powers.

questions.question: What inference are readers expected to make from the order in nature?
questions.answer: They should understand that Allah alone governs all affairs.

questions.question: Why is the example of human struggle over power included?
questions.answer: It gives a familiar example showing that even limited authority resists being shared.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast human weakness with Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Humans are needy and weak yet still guard small authority, while Allah has complete power and supreme rule.

questions.question: What warning about belief is built into this argument?
questions.answer: Thinking Allah has partners goes against the order of the universe and the meaning of true sovereignty.

questions.question: What does the opening of the passage invite a person to do?
questions.answer: It invites a person to look at the universe carefully and thoughtfully.

questions.question: What two images are used for the cosmos in the first paragraph?
questions.answer: A thriving kingdom and a wisely managed city.

questions.question: What do these images suggest about random chance in the universe?
questions.answer: They suggest the universe is not random but directed with wisdom and control.

questions.question: How are the different parts of creation linked together in the passage?
questions.answer: They are shown as parts of one system, each doing its own role under one authority.

questions.question: What special role do commands, orders, and laws play in the argument?
questions.answer: They show that creation runs by binding rule, not by separate independent powers.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both the lowest soldier and the highest commander?
questions.answer: To show that one authority covers every level without exception.

questions.question: What is the effect of several rulers trying to direct the same matter?
questions.answer: Their rivalry would bring disorder and spoil proper management.

questions.question: How does the passage use examples from both nature and society?
questions.answer: It combines scenes from creation with examples of kings and local leaders to make the idea easier to grasp.

questions.question: What proof from observation is stronger in this passage: chaos or order?
questions.answer: Order is the proof, because it is what we truly see all around us.

questions.question: Why is the dignity of sovereignty important in this discussion?
questions.answer: Because high rule is presented as something too noble to accept a competing partner.

questions.question: What lesson is drawn from people harming even relatives for worldly control?
questions.answer: It shows that the desire to rule strongly rejects sharing, even in weak human beings.

questions.question: How does the passage end its argument in a respectful scholarly way?
questions.answer: It says fuller proofs exist elsewhere and sends the reader there for more detail.

questions.question: What central claim does this passage make about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: Allah’s rule is complete, universal, and not shared with anyone.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the condition of the universe as a whole?
questions.answer: It describes it as active, productive, orderly, and firmly governed.

questions.question: Why is this description important for understanding tawhid?
questions.answer: Because it supports the belief that one Lord is managing everything in unity.

questions.question: What does the military language add to the passage’s meaning?
questions.answer: It highlights discipline, command, ranks, and obedience throughout creation.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are included under this command structure?
questions.answer: Everything from atoms to plants, animals, and stars.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea is used to reject the belief in many gods?
questions.answer: If multiple gods controlled the same world, the natural result would be corruption and disorder.

questions.question: How does the passage support that idea with human examples?
questions.answer: It shows that even human communities become unstable when more than one top ruler competes for control.

questions.question: What opposite condition do we actually witness in the universe?
questions.answer: We witness balance, arrangement, and dependable order.

questions.question: What does that observed order tell us about Allah’s affairs?
questions.answer: It tells us no partner is interfering in them.

questions.question: Why is human violence over small authority a strong comparison?
questions.answer: It makes readers see how strongly even tiny ownership of power resists sharing.

questions.question: What greater truth is inferred about Allah from that comparison?
questions.answer: His absolute power and sacred rule make partnership impossible.

questions.question: In one sentence, summarize the logic of the whole passage.
questions.answer: Since the universe is perfectly ordered under one majestic rule, Allah alone is its sovereign with no partner.

questions.question: What title is given to the truth discussed in this section?
questions.answer: Sovereignty.

questions.question: What kind of person will notice the lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: A person who studies the universe with broad and careful attention.

questions.question: In the first paragraph, what does the behavior of all species show?
questions.answer: It shows they are carrying out set tasks within an ordered system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning armies in the heavens and earth?
questions.answer: It is to show that all creation is under one commanding authority.

questions.question: How does the passage connect tiny creatures and huge celestial bodies?
questions.answer: It presents both as equally subject to the same rule and command.

questions.question: What would be the result if more than one independent ruler handled the same creation?
questions.answer: The result would be confusion, breakdown, and loss of order.

questions.question: What political comparisons help readers picture that breakdown?
questions.answer: The examples of two kings over one country and two headmen over one district.

questions.question: What real-world evidence disproves the idea of shared divine control?
questions.answer: The consistent order seen in everything from insect parts to the heavens.

questions.question: Why does the passage say sovereignty has dignity?
questions.answer: Because rulership is presented as a lofty station that does not accept competition.

questions.question: How is man used as a lesser example in the argument?
questions.answer: Even though humans are weak and needy, they still fight fiercely over small temporary power.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude about the Lord of all creation?
questions.answer: He would never let anyone take part in His sacred and absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: How should this passage strengthen a Muslim student’s understanding of shirk?
questions.answer: It shows that shirk opposes the order of creation and the truth that Allah alone rules everything.
